evidence_class: CONTAINER EVIDENCE, NOT PRODUCTION. Same throwaway Docker method as tools/server-performance-qualification.json and tools/outbox-replay.qualification.json (compose project hmem-perftest, loopback only); the live system was not contacted.
outcome: At production pool defaults (main 15, delivery 10, GHC -N) HEAD f206ff72 passes the measured parts of all eight combined gates (replay cut and revocation not re-verified) against the matched 7127a3d9 baseline: pooled foreground p95 1.078, every route <= 1.035, seeded capture append 0.567, and the stuck catch-up retires only the blocked owner while all four healthy hot sockets stay open and receive every write. The scope-lock ablation does not improve foreground latency (pooled 1.158, two routes over +10%), so it does not confirm scope locks as a cause; with no per-route regression left on HEAD there is nothing for it to explain at these settings.
owner: Tasks 033d1704 and 17e8cd32 developer through review; parent 073d6bfb owns final combined re-qualification
retention: Retain this compact receipt until 073d6bfb closes or a later matched rerun supersedes it. Raw run summaries, the seed manifest, scratch sources, build logs, secrets and the reduction scripts were task scratch and were removed at teardown.

before.build: git archive of 7127a3d9 with the HEAD Dockerfile plus two COPY lines restoring the 7127a3d9 hmem-core.cabal, hmem-server/package.yaml and hmem-server.cabal after a Stack dependency layer resolved from 8d5101d0 package metadata (identical to HEAD package metadata). The hmem-server binary hash equals the before image of tools/outbox-replay.qualification.json.

after.build: git archive of HEAD with the repository Dockerfile

ablation.patch: MEASUREMENT ONLY, UNSAFE, NOT FOR COMMIT. hmem-core/src/HMem/DB/ChangeStream.hs: readReplayWindow (readReplayScanPage), acknowledgeReplayWithExpiry (acknowledgeReplayScan) and rebaseResumeTokenAfterHidden, the three calls the WebSocket canonical delivery path makes, replace SELECT ... FROM hmem_change_stream_lock($1,$2) with a plain SELECT authorization_epoch, next_cursor, retained_from_cursor FROM change_stream_scope_counters (same predicate, same columns, one round trip, falling back to the lock only if the row is missing). Ticket validation, HTTP replay, snapshots and retention keep the lock.
ablation.why_it_isolates: Each per-socket transaction keeps its statements, bearer row lock (FOR UPDATE on the resume token), authorization check and outbox read; only the scope-row INSERT ... ON CONFLICT and FOR UPDATE are gone, so per-socket delivery neither waits behind scope writers nor blocks them.
ablation.guarantees_dropped: Serialization of replay pages and acknowledgements against authorization-epoch changes (revocation) and against retention pruning, which takes the same scope lock; a page could pass authority checks across a concurrent revocation or miss records pruned mid-read.

environment.seed: A fresh volume seeded with perftest.mjs through the after image: 6 planning workspaces (1,500 projects, 9,153 tasks, 12,000 Observations); 562 terminated sessions (3,271,093,120 raw bytes, all 562 archives ready) and 12 active (347,544,869 bytes) in 33,825 chunks; 7,100 API task updates cloned 25 times and spread over 90 days. 5,023,069,875-byte database, 412,149 audit rows, 77,149 outbox rows (hot workspace counter 10,140). CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements was run on the seed before the stopped volume (6,123,522,560 bytes) was copied once to hmem-perftest-pgdata-base; every run restored that copy (same byte count each time).

method.matching: Same seed copy, workload definition, compose file and host for all variants; each run starts a fresh server on a freshly restored volume. Counterbalanced order before-1, after-1, abl-1, abl-2, after-2, before-2 (mean position 3.5 each). Gates compare the mean of each variant's two runs with the before mean, as in the earlier receipts.
method.workload: combined.mjs defaults (30 s idle, 120 s contention, 8 s stuck catch-up hold); see tools/server-performance-qualification.json method.workload.
method.measurement: Client latency from the host. Database counts are pg_stat_statements calls per phase: outbox_scan = FROM change_stream_outbox, scope_lock = hmem_change_stream_lock (top-level statements only; writers take the lock inside plpgsql). Pool counters are health deltas per phase for pool (main) and delivery_pool. Pool wait share = mean db_wait_ms / mean complete_ms over the slowest 5% of joined foreground requests (main pool; the before image has no request phases or pool counters).

scope_lock_per_contention_phase.note: Ablation residue is snapshot locking only (2 statements). Its replacement read was not counted: the runner truncates statement text to 160 characters before matching and the marker comment lies beyond that. Replay-authority calls, one per per-socket transaction, show those transactions still ran: after 3,067-3,167, ablation 2,355-2,583, before 475-993.

observations.regime: Heavy routes (task_update_fields 349-463 ms, nav_root 282-292 ms, search_unified 156-317 ms at p95) are slower in every variant than in tools/outbox-replay.qualification.json, and before pooled p95 is 151-158 ms against 88-96 ms there. That receipt ran before with 10 connections and on another day; this one cannot separate pool size from host state. after cheap reads (task_get 5.5-5.8 ms, planning_counts 5.7-5.8 ms) are faster than both before here and before there (7.6 and 7.7 ms).

conclusions.stuck_case_on_head_15_10: PASS in both after runs (033d1704 acceptance: healthy sockets in other scopes keep every write and are not retired; the stuck owner is retired and reclaimed; the drain is clean).
conclusions.per_route_on_head: PASS: no route above 1.035 (ratio of means); also within the limit against the faster before run alone.
conclusions.scope_lock_ablation: Not confirmed. Removing the per-socket scope locks (3,067-3,167 calls and 13.4-15.6 s per phase down to 48 snapshot calls) leaves cheap-read p95 equal to after and does not reduce pooled or heavy-route p95 (ablation pooled 1.158, task_update_fields 1.143, search_unified 1.21; abl-1 is the slowest run of the set). At these settings HEAD has no per-route regression for the ablation to explain, and this receipt does not attribute the earlier pool-10 regression to any cause.

limitations: Two runs per variant on one shared host. before-1 cheap reads were 2-8x slower than before-2, so per-route before means are inflated; the faster-run-only comparison is reported and still passes for after.
search_unified p95 ranges 156-317 ms across runs of every variant; its gate margin is within run-to-run spread.
The before image ran with 15 connections because the compose file now pins production defaults; earlier receipts used 10, so absolute numbers are not comparable across receipts.

The runner copy differs from tools/perftest/combined.mjs in output only (recorded diff hash); the workload definition is unchanged. Its ablation statement class missed every call because of statement-text truncation.
The stuck case for the ablation is not evidence: the ablation removes the lock wait the case depends on.
after-1 had one HTTP 500 on a shell resync under contention; logs were on tmpfs and its cause was not captured.
Closed-loop foreground clients: completed requests per run were 12,902-13,103 (before), 12,801-13,380 (after) and 11,370-13,049 (ablation); hot writes were open-loop and matched (1,914-1,920).
Delivery latency starts at the write response, so it is a lower bound; RSS is sampled once per second.
Local authentication makes every principal the trusted superadmin; revocation and per-user reauthorization rely on focused specs, which were not run here. The replay cut was not re-verified.
Admission limits were not approached (27 sockets in one audience). MCP follower diagnostics were not collected.
